pretreatments.description: Wet sieving with tap water to remove smaller and coarser impurities
Drying at 45 ± 3 °C to a constant weight over two days
Determination of moisture, total solids (TS), and volatile solids (VS) contents according to the NREL LAP for biomass and total dissolved solids of liquid process samples
Determination of ash content according to NREL LAP for determination of ash in biomass
Enzymatic liquefaction and saccharification of the duckweed was performed in four 2-L flasks with 1 L total working volume
Prior to liquefaction, 50 g duckweed (dry weight) was sterilized by autoclaving with 945 ml water for 30 min at 121 °C
pH was adjusted to 7.0 ± 0.1 with 2 M hydrochloric acid
α-amylase (Sigma Aldrich, A3403, USA) was added at a loading of 5000 units g starch^−1
Glucoamylase (Sigma Aldrich, 10115, USA) and cellulase (Novozymes, Cellic® CTec2, Denmark) were added to each flask
Saccharification was then performed at 50 °C, while mixing at 120 rpm for 24 h
Liquid hot water pretreatment was carried out in a 500 ml stainless steel Parr reactor (Parr Instrument Company, model 4575, Moline, IL), with a pressure limit of 345 bar
The vessel was filled with 30 g duckweed (dry weight) and 270 g distilled water
The temperature was ramped up to 150 °C within 15 min, followed by pressurization with nitrogen gas for 5 min which was monitored using a digital pressure transducer
